around.headline: H1N1 outbreak shuts down classes at a Bengaluru school
around.summary: Over 500 students at Clarence High fell sick with flu symptoms, forcing the school to suspend offline classes for two days. If your child shows fever or flu symptoms, keep them home and get tested rather than sending them in.

around.headline: State food-safety crackdown finds rats, cockroaches, expired meat in Bengaluru kitchens
around.summary: A statewide drive inspected 1,849 food establishments and sent over 2,400 samples for testing, turning up unhygienic kitchens at several outlets. Worth checking a restaurant's FSSAI hygiene rating before ordering, especially from lesser-known outlets.

around.headline: Metro's 19-km Blue Line faces fresh delay as ORR roadwork could clash with construction
around.summary: Overlapping Metro and Outer Ring Road works threaten to push back the already-delayed Blue Line further and could double up commute disruption along the corridor. If you travel this stretch, expect longer detours in the coming months.

around.headline: Bengaluru Traffic Police book 517 drunk-driving cases in a week-long drive
around.summary: A week-long enforcement push logged 517 drunk-driving cases across the city. Expect more checkpoints on weekend nights — keep a backup ride option if you're drinking.

around.headline: Post-Freedom Habba cleanup: 20 tonnes of waste cleared around Vidhana Soudha
around.summary: BBMP crews cleared 20 tonnes of waste left behind after the city's Freedom Habba celebrations, while Metro admitted the event caused commuter chaos and crowding at nearby stations. If you're headed that way this evening, expect residual congestion around Vidhana Soudha.

around.headline: Supreme Court directs Karnataka to comply with Cauvery water-release orders to Tamil Nadu
around.summary: The Supreme Court asked Karnataka to fall in line with the Cauvery Water Management Authority's directions on releasing water downstream to Tamil Nadu. Karnataka's own irrigation and drinking-water supply could tighten if larger releases are enforced through the dry months ahead.

street_smart.title: A traffic constable flags you down for a signal jump and asks for your licence. You're already late and irritated — what do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Real incident today: a JD(S) leader was arrested after grabbing a Bengaluru traffic constable by the collar and kicking him for being pulled over — caught on video and widely shared (The Hindu, NDTV, The Indian Express).
street_smart.situation: The constable is polite but firm, writing up an e-challan on his handheld device. You're stressed about being late and feel the stop is unfair.

choices.text: Raise your voice, claim you know someone senior in the department, and try to talk your way out of the ticket.
choices.feedback: Bluffing or name-dropping rarely works on a constable doing his job, and it can tip into obstruction if you get aggressive. It wastes your time and his without changing the outcome.

choices.text: Grab the constable's collar or push past him to leave without the challan.
choices.feedback: This is exactly what happened today — and it ended in an on-camera arrest. Assaulting or obstructing a public servant on duty is a cognizable offence; the video goes viral within hours and the legal and reputational fallout is far worse than any traffic fine.

choices.text: Hand over your licence and RC, accept the e-challan, and pay or contest it later through the proper channel.
choices.feedback: Correct. Comply on the spot regardless of how you feel about the stop — that's non-negotiable. If you think the challan is wrong, you can dispute it afterward through the Bengaluru Traffic Police portal or in traffic court, with your dashcam or any recording as evidence.

choices.text: Drive off before the constable finishes writing up the challan.
choices.feedback: Fleeing a traffic stop can be treated as evading a public servant and invites a chase or a more serious charge than the original violation. It also leaves the original challan unresolved and accumulating.

takeaways: Never make physical contact with a police officer, even in anger — assaulting a public servant on duty is a cognizable offence that leads to swift arrest, as seen today.
If you believe a challan is wrong, don't argue on the spot — contest it afterward via the Bengaluru Traffic Police portal (btp.gov.in) or in traffic court, ideally with dashcam footage.
If an officer behaves improperly, note their badge number and file a complaint through the official Traffic Police helpline instead of escalating in person.

quiz.why: The 19-km Blue Line was already running behind schedule; overlapping ORR works threaten to push commuter disruption even further out.

quiz.question: How many drunk-driving cases did Bengaluru Traffic Police book in a single week-long crackdown reported today?
quiz.why: The week-long drive is part of a broader push on road-safety enforcement across the city.

quiz.question: The Supreme Court today asked Karnataka to comply with the Cauvery Water Management Authority's directions on releasing water to which state?
quiz.why: The Cauvery water-sharing dispute between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu has been contested for decades and is periodically arbitrated by the Supreme Court and the CWMA.

quiz.question: In banking, the 'repo rate' is best described as the rate at which:
options: The RBI lends short-term funds to commercial banks
Banks charge customers on personal loans
Fixed deposits earn guaranteed annual returns
quiz.why: Changes in the repo rate ripple through to the loan and deposit rates banks offer ordinary customers, which is why RBI policy announcements get so much coverage.

quiz.question: During CPR, chest compressions should be given at roughly what rate?
quiz.why: This is the pace recommended by resuscitation guidelines — roughly the tempo of the song 'Stayin' Alive', which is often used to train the rhythm.
